XXVII.|OF THE APOSTLES.|369}}</noinclude>that day vvere come. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=30}}† But as the shipmen sought to flee out of the ship, hauing let dovvne the cock-boate into the sea, pretending as if they vvere about to cast out ankers out of the fore part of the ship, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=31}}† Paul said to the Centurion and to the souldiars, {{sup|‖}} Vnles these tarie in the ship, you can not be saued. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=32}}† Then the souldiars cut of the ropes of the cock-boate: and suffered it to fal avvay.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=33}}† And vvhen it began to be light, Paul desired all to take meate, saying, This day is the fourtenth day that you expect and remaine fasting, taking nothing. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=34}}† For the vvhich cause I desire you to take meate for your health sake: for there shal not an heare of the head perish of any of you. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=35}}† And vvhen he had said these things, taking bread, he gaue thankes to God in the sight of them al: and vvhen he had broken it, he began to eate. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=36}}† And being al made of better cheere, they also tooke meate. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=37}}† And vve vvere in al in the ship, soules tvvo hundred seuentie sixe. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=38}}† And being filled vvith meate, they lighted the ship, casting the vvheat into the sea. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=39}}† And vvhen day vvas come, they knevv not the land: but they spied a certaine creeke that had a shore, into the vvhich they minded, if they could, to cast a land the ship. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=40}}† And vvhen they had taken vp the ankers, they committed them selues to the sea, loosing vvithal the rudder bands: and hoising vp the maine saile according as the vvinde blevve, they vvent on tovvard the shore. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=41}}† And vvhen vve vvere fallen into a place betvvene tvvo seas, they graueled the ship: and the fore-part truly sticking fast remained vnmoueable: but the hinder part vvas broken by the violence of the sea. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=42}}† And the counsel of the souldiars vvas, that they should kil the prisoners: lest any svvimming out, might runne avvay. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=43}}† But the Centurion vvilling to saue Paul, forbade it to be done: & he commaunded them that could svvimme, to cast out them selues first, and escape, and goe forth to land: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=44}}† and the rest, some they caried on bordes, and some vpon those things that vvere of the ship. And so it came to passe, that al the soules escaped to land.
